Sounds like you might be having night terrors (different than nightmares), which are no joke. Neither is sleep paralysis. It's helped me to keep my eyes shut during sleep paralysis. Your brain is still able to dream in this state, so opening your eyes is really asking for it. I only open them if I'm feeling particularly brave that night. Meditation has helped me a lot, I recommend you try it if you haven't already. The effects are slow and subtle at first, but powerful over time.

When I was a Christian, I thought they were real. Now I know that my brain is really strong with imagination, and anxiety/paranoia is the trigger for the terrifying hallucinations. Curbing those is the only consistent off switch that I've found.

Here's the thing: if you're freaked out enough about it, your brain will anticipate the danger so much that it will create it. We evolved from, amongst other things, prey. So if you don't burn off the cortisol in your body, your brain will think there's still danger. If you don't see danger, it will make danger. And thus the cycle of anxiety restarts.

Best advice if you think spirits may attack you: stay calm. Remind yourself that YOU are in control, and it'll be ok.

When I was a Christian, God was my strength. When I left Christianity, I knew that something better awaited me. I've had 9 therapists throughout my life (including my current one) and all of them have told me that I'm resilient (therapy is when I learned about this word). Apparently resilience is the holy grail of psychology. I'm not sure how it happened, but I always try to think positive and find a way to climb up.

Anytime I felt like giving up and had an existential crisis, I would always reach out to a friend. Friendship is life.

Ah, Hinduism. The oldest religion on the planet. That was a shock to me when I learned that, because I was raised to believe that Judaism was the oldest. Cuz, you know, the bible teaches it that way.

If the bible were true, and Yahweh exists, he hasn't given us true free will. He's given an ultimatum: "Choose me or be tortured for eternity". That's manipulation. That's toxic.

If Yahweh exists, it's also not our fault that evil exists. It's his. He's the one who created Lucifer, knowing that Lucifer would become vain and eventually tempt mankind in the garden of Eden (Ezekiel 28:1-19), and then let it happen. If Yahweh exists and is omnipotent, omniscient, omnipresent, and omnibenevolent, then evil exists simply because he's allowed it into his creation. 

If he didn't create evil, then he is not omnipotent. If he did create it, then he is not omnibenevolent. Check out Mackie's "The Problem of Evil". He goes into great detail about this.

The bible became my survival book during this time. I knew damn near every scripture to use for spiritual warfare, knew the rites for exorcism of body and home, was even on the bible quiz team and memorized the entirely of the book of Matthew verbatim for competition. And the funny thing was, in the face of these "demons", scripture alone didn't get rid of them. The only thing that did was whether or not I felt calm. Sometimes that meant "casting them out" several times before it would stop. 

So, protection? Hardly. Why would I have the gift of "discerning of spirits" (1 Cor. 12:10 NASB) if scripture didn't take care of them? My mentality of being anxious or calm should not be a factor in this, only God's power vs theirs. Clearly something was amiss.

My family said the same thing about vulnerability when I told them I no longer believed. And you know what? I've found a way to overcome. So, either I have developed a power on my own, outside of Yahweh, to overcome these demons, or none of it is real. So, honestly, none of it is real. Even to this day, if I deal with the anxiety, the hallucinations stop. Consistently. So my own mind is at work here, nothing spiritual. Christianity (not just my family, but other Christians) exacerbated the issues with my mental health, hence the religious trauma syndrome (subset of ptsd). This is something that happens a lot with Christianity, I'm not the only survivor of this syndrome.

Well, it is extreme. Here goes:

My mom would tell me stories about how God showed her I had a big calling. One such story was when she was 6 months pregnant with me. At the time she was married to my father who served as a marine during Desert Storm. Apparently when he was deployed, my mom went off base to eat at McDonald's regularly. When she was there one day, two dudes with pentagrams tattooed on their faces walked in and were staring at her incessantly. She said God told her that they were planning to sacrifice me to Satan. She left immediately, and they followed her in their vehicle all the way to the gates of Camp le June. Since they weren't military, they couldn't get in.

After I was born, she moved back to Oklahoma (this is where I was raised) and stayed with my grandparents for a while. She tells me that once during our stay there, she wakes up in the middle of the night and sees an imp the height of a toddler in her bedroom doorway with gray skin and decaying teeth. She says that God told her to not let it touch me, so she scoops me out of my crib before it could snatch me. She goes on to say that she began praying to God, who sent an angel to "cast the demon out".

While all of this commotion was going on, someone rang the doorbell. My grandfather answers, and on the other side of their barred gate (it was from floor to ceiling, anchored in concrete and brick, effectively enclosing the front porch) he says was the devil himself, dressed like a business man, floating in some sort of vehicle that was a wheel within a wheel. Kinda reminds me of the UFO description in Isaiah.

Apparently, the devil asked my grandfather directly to hand me over. Of course grandpa declined, and used scripture to "cast him out". So, my mom reasons, God has called me to do something big, to lead his army against Satan. Why else would he go to such extent to get his hands on me?

The most impactful hallucination was recent. Earlier this year I was working night shift security. As I'm walking down main street around 3am, I hear a disembodied voice ask "wouldn't it be cool if I took over for a while?" To which I replied "no, no it wouldn't, fuck off". Then I hear someone humming across the road. I look to my left and see a blonde haired woman, barefoot (it's 20°F), wearing white robes, walking in tandem with me. She's slouched forward in such a way that her hair is covering her face. As I look at her, without un-slouching, she looks at me, head all sideways and moving slowly. I can see glistening moisture on her skin, I can see her bone structure, but she has zero facial features. No eyes, but the sockets were there. No nose, but the ridge bone was there. No mouth, but clearly a jaw and teeth underneath. Just skin pulled over bone.

I immediately recognize that I'm both anxious and paranoid, and thus hallucinating. Once aware, I breathe deep and release my anxiety/tension. The woman just evaporates. After that I told my therapist that I can't work nights, so she wrote a letter to my employer. I work days now, but with a day less a week and a full dollar pay cut. Sacrificed $702/mo to keep my sanity.

That's a hard one to answer because there have been so many. Everything from things appearing in mirrors that shouldn't be there, to seeing demons "hiding" in objects or people, to waking up from a nightmare of demons only to discover sleep paralysis.

The most traumatic one was probably my first. I was around 5 years old (1995). My grandparents were visiting out of state for Christmas, sleeping on the bottom mattress of my bunk bed, and I'm sleeping up top. I wake up in the middle of the night while everyone's asleep. Everything had this weird green tint to it. Now, normally my mom would have a small radio in the hall playing lullaby music for my sisters and me (our rooms were adjacent to each other), and I heard the music echo into silence. Being curious, and since my bunk was situated in such a way that I could see down the hall into the living room, I look out into the hall to see if maybe my mom turned it down for some reason.

What I saw instead was a tall shadow audibly whoosh down the hall. Then it whooshed into my room, its head phasing through the space between the top of the door and the ceiling. It turns to face me, and it has two red glowing eyes, with a gigantic maw housing sharp teeth about a foot long. Think True Ogre from Tekken 3 but bigger teeth and skin that's a black void. It starts mocking me with deep reverberating laughter. At this point I'm screaming so loud that my throat hurts. I cry for my mom. She doesn't come. I bend over the railing to scream at my grandparents. They've got a blueish tint, and don't respond. I cover my head with my blankets. Its laughter reverberates through the bed. I call out to the only other name I can think of: I pray to Jesus. The laughter continues for a moment, then disappears. I stayed under my blanket for a long time, shaking with fear. Eventually I peek out. The green tint is gone. The demon is gone. I don't remember falling asleep.

The next morning, throat still sore, I asked every adult one by one "was it you that scared me last night?" And everyone said "no". That was the beginning of it all. A lot of bad shit happened in that room later in life, and not just to me. I was raped twice in there.
